To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DNA-bound PCNAs are sufficient for strand discrimination and that MutSα inhibits the unloading of PCNAs, thereby extending the post-replicative temporal window permissive for strand-specific MMR (Figure 1).

DNA synthesis induces the strand-specific mismatch repair (MMRs) capability and that MSH2/MSH6, which is the eukaryotic MutSα, maintains the MMRs capability after the disappearance of the signal by inhibiting PCNAs unloading from DNA.

DNA-bound PCNA enables strand-specific MMR after the disappearance of DNA strand discontinuities and MutSα inhibits PCNA unloading, thereby extending significantly this temporal window permissive for strand-specific MMR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of mismatch repair, a DNA repair pathway that corrects errors in newly synthesized DNA.
understanding how DNA mismatch repair works and what is its role in genome integrity and stability.
understanding how the cell ensures that mismatch repair is limited to a temporal window during which DNA replication is complete.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MutSα maintains the MMR capacity in Xenopus egg extracts by inhibiting PCN unloading.
MutSα is required for the maintenance of the post-replication MMR capability by inhibiting the unloading of PCNA.
The MMR capability must therefore be limited to a window of time during which the signals that enable strand discrimination are available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA-bound PCNAA is a signal that enables the strand discrimination after the strand discontinuities are removed.
we discovered a novel role of the MMR protein, MutSα, in the retention of strand-specific mismatch repair (MMRx).
we discovered a novel function of the MMR factor MutSα in maintaining the post-replicative MMR capability, by inhibiting PCNAs unloading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the post-replicative temporal window for mismatch repair (MM) is maintained by the inhibition of PCNA unloading from the DNA by MutSα.
the MMR capability is not only limited to a postreplicative temporal window, but also limited to a post-synthetic temporal window.
the post-replicational mismatch repair (MM) capability is maintained by MutSα through the inhibition of PCNA unloading from the newly synthesized DNA.
